title: Guard FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl link/reauth methods against silent no-op on null currentUser
why: If currentUser is null when these fire (expired/revoked anonymous session, or a UI race), the `?.` swallows the call and the method returns a normally-completed Future<void> — no exception, no signal that nothing happened. The one real caller (features/account/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:129-140 `linkGoogleProvider`/`linkEmailProvider`/`reauthenticateWithGoogle`) just awaits and reports success with nothing to double-check. That directly undercuts AU-1: linking must actually run against the anonymous uid so its offline data carries over; a silent no-op leaves the account anonymous while the user believes it's now permanent, and Identity Platform auto-deletes unlinked anonymous accounts after 30 days (AU-3's rationale), which can permanently orphan the child's offline learning history. Every sibling precondition check in this same file (deleteCurrentUser:172-176, updatePassword:181-186, reauthenticateWithEmail:192-199, sendEmailVerification:100-104) throws `StateError` instead of silently no-op'ing; the one genuinely-intentional no-op in the file (`updateDisplayName`) is declared as such by an explicit 'is a no-op when no user is signed in' test — these three methods have neither the guard nor a test declaring the no-op intentional, which is the tell that it's an oversight, not a design choice.
recommendation: Add the same `if (user == null) throw ...` guard used elsewhere in this file before calling linkWithCredential/reauthenticateWithCredential in all three methods (ideally throwing the typed exception recommended in the companion EH-5 finding rather than another StateError). Add regression tests mirroring the existing 'throws when no user is signed in' pattern for linkWithGoogleIdToken, linkWithEmailAndPassword, and reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken.
acceptance_criteria: linkWithGoogleIdToken, linkWithEmailAndPassword, and reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken throw (not silently no-op) when currentUser is null.
New red-first unit tests in firebase_auth_gateway_impl_test.dart cover the null-currentUser case for all 3 methods and pass.
Existing 'links credential when signed in' tests for the same methods stay green.

corrections: The "one real caller ... just awaits and reports success" framing is wrong for 2 of 3 sites: linkWithGoogleIdToken/linkWithEmailAndPassword are dead code with no UI entry point in lib/ (only exercised by unit tests). The 3rd (reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken) is live but its only real call path guarantees currentUser is non-null, and the downstream deleteCurrentUser() call already guards null with a thrown StateError, so the claimed silent-orphan-account scenario has no actual path through the app today. The defect (missing guard, inconsistent with sibling methods) is real and worth fixing defensively, but severity should be P2 (design debt/defensive hygiene), not P1 (user-visible defect).

Downgrade from P1 to P2 (design debt, not currently user-visible) and CONFIRMED to SUSPECTED. 2 of the 3 cited sites (lines 218, 238 — linkWithGoogleIdToken/linkWithEmailAndPassword) are dead code with no UI caller anywhere in lib/ (no Link Account screen exists). The 1 reachable site (line 226, reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken, called from account_actions.dart:286) is guarded downstream by Firebase's server-side recent-login enforcement in deleteCurrentUser(), which is caught and surfaced as an error rather than causing silent corruption/security bypass. The underlying code smell (missing null guard vs. sibling pattern) is real and worth fixing before the link feature ships, but the P0-adjacent 'orphans child's offline learning history' consequence described in 'why' is not reachable today.
